headline: From Tragedy to Protection: New Car Seat Sticker Saves Lives in Emergencies
meta_description: After losing her sister in a highway pile-up, a woman created the Roth ID Tag—a car seat sticker that doubles as a hospital bracelet to protect children in eme…
summary_short: A sister transformed personal tragedy into a lifesaving invention: a car seat sticker that becomes an emergency ID bracelet, endorsed by first responders nationwide.
body:
When a 47-car pile-up devastated the Ohio Turnpike on December 23rd, 2022, Julie Roth did not survive the worst winter storm that year. Her two young children, Ayla and Rory, strapped into their car seats, did. Yet as first responders pulled them from the wreckage and rushed them to the hospital, a critical problem emerged: no one knew who these traumatized children were. Hours passed before their identities were established, before medical questions could be answered, and before their father received the news. Julie's sister channeled that anguish into something concrete—the Roth ID Tag, an adhesive sticker designed to live permanently on a child's car seat, containing emergency medical and contact information that parents write in advance. When crisis strikes, the sticker tears away to become an instant hospital bracelet, eliminating the chaos that nearly swallowed Ayla and Rory in their darkest hours.

The innovation fills a genuine gap in child safety. A QR code on the tag allows responders to access additional information if the child is registered through the Roth ID Tag website, ensuring continuity of care even when verbal communication is impossible. The design has been approved by registered Child Passenger Safety Technicians under Safe Kids Worldwide and has earned recognition for solving a problem no one had quite addressed until now.

What began as one family's unimaginable loss has rippled outward. Captain Wilhelm of the Bellevue Fire Department praised the product, noting how it would have transformed countless emergency scenarios. Sheriff, fire, and police departments across multiple states now officially endorse it, alongside highway safety boards and departments of transportation. The Roth ID Tag is available through major retailers including Target, Walmart, and Amazon—a tangible legacy of love and purpose born from grief.
quick_facts: Julie Roth died in a 47-car pile-up on Ohio Turnpike, December 23, 2022
Her two children survived but went unidentified for hours in hospital
Roth ID Tag: adhesive car seat sticker that becomes emergency hospital bracelet
Endorsed by fire departments, police, and highway safety boards across multiple states
Available at Target, Walmart, and Amazon nationally
